title: Ras Frostwhisper: a lich’s mortality
summary: A magistrate seeks a relic of Ras Frostwhisper’s mortal life. Stromgarde, Light’s Hope, Stratholme and Scholomance lead to Leonid’s account and an attempt to bind the lich to his former self.
opening: A ruined city yields a small remnant; an old witness gives it a history. Bound to the soul of a fallen mage, the keepsake carries a mortal memory toward the lich in Scholomance.

chapters.title: A remnant of mortal life
chapters.body:
At Caer Darrow, Magistrate Marduke appeared to those who could see the dead. He sought a way into Ras Frostwhisper’s mortal past. A keepsake from Stromgarde, the ruined city he called Ras’s home, might give that lost life a hold upon the present. Before the lich could be confronted, something of the man he had been had to be found.

Among Stromgarde’s broken stones, the seeker searched for a possession from Ras’s human life. The fallen city held the beginning of another man’s history beneath its own ruin. A small surviving object might reach where force alone could not. Beyond the abandoned walls waited the lich, whose old home could still yield a memory he had left behind.

A keepsake survived among the ruins. Marduke believed it could help create an artifact capable of reaching Ras. Its value lay in the life it recalled rather than the strength of its making. Carried toward Light’s Hope Chapel, the small possession joined a fallen city to the hope that a bond with the mortal past might endure beneath undeath.

At Light’s Hope Chapel, Leonid Barthalomew received the keepsake. Marduke had heard that Ras surrendered himself in Stratholme; Leonid might know more. The search had reached a witness among those who understood the dead. Before the token could serve its purpose, the seeker needed to learn how the man of Stromgarde had become the lich they meant to face.

chapters.title: A witness and a tainted ground
chapters.body:
Leonid remembered Ras pledging his soul to the Lich King and ending his own mortal life. His body fell upon marked ground. In Leonid’s recollection, the Lich King stood over the fallen mage, and Ras rose as a lich. The witness’s memory gave the old rumor a terrible shape, binding the keepsake’s human past to a chosen surrender.

Leonid named the place Menethil’s Gift: ground blessed by the Lich King and held holy by the Scourge. The name carried a bitter inheritance. He sent the seeker back to Stratholme with the keepsake, toward the place where Ras had yielded his mortal life. There the small possession might gain a bond with the soul its memory recalled.

At Menethil’s Gift, the keepsake was placed upon the tainted ground. A soul could cling to what recalled its former life, and the object became bound to that fallen soul. Its change offered the means the search had sought. Yet the bond had not been tested against Ras, and the hope carried from Stromgarde still awaited its encounter with the lich.

The Soulbound Keepsake returned to Light’s Hope. Leonid believed its connection to the fallen soul should also hold to Ras’s physical form. The object had changed; whether it could reach the lich remained to be learned. He sent it onward to Marduke, carrying an explanation and a possibility toward the magistrate whose inquiry had begun among memories of a mortal home.

At Caer Darrow, Marduke received the transformed keepsake and prepared the seeker for its use. The search could now turn toward Scholomance. From ruined streets, a witness’s memory and tainted ground, the living had gathered a means to confront Ras through his own past. The old academy sheltered the lich whose human life the object still recalled.

chapters.title: The lich and the keepsake
chapters.body:
Within Scholomance’s cold halls, the seeker found Ras Frostwhisper. The keepsake was brought within reach of the mage who had chosen undeath. All that had been gathered now met the form it was meant to change. A possession from Stromgarde’s ruins stood against the power that had carried its former owner beyond his mortal life.

The keepsake reached Ras through the bond with his former life. His undead form gave way to a mortal one. The change opened a brief and terrible possibility; it did not offer a restored life beyond the encounter. The man recalled by the token could be struck down, and Marduke’s purpose now approached its final cost.

Ras was killed in mortal form, and his head was carried back to Marduke. The keepsake had undone his undead guise long enough for that blow to fall. What became of his spirit remained unknown. From the ruined home to Scholomance’s cold halls, the search had recovered a bond with the past and used it for a reckoning rather than a return to life.

At Caer Darrow, Marduke received the head and declared that ten thousand restless souls had cried out at the blow against the Scourge. His words gave the deed its meaning, while Ras’s own soul remained beyond the seeker’s knowledge. The lich had been made mortal and killed. The inquiry ended with the magistrate’s declaration, leaving the dead their unanswered silence.
